info.name: wsoftblog-v2 API
info.description:
REST API for the W Labs blog (Payload CMS 3.89 on Next.js, Postgres). Covers auth plus core CRUD for `posts`, `media`, and `users`, and the two legacy wire-compat endpoints the Nuxt marketing site consumes.

## Setup
1. Import the companion environment file (`wsoftblog-v2.local.postman_environment.json`) and select it.
2. Point `baseUrl` at your running server (default `http://localhost:3000` — must match `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL` in `.env` **exactly**, see below).
3. Run **00 · Auth → Login** once. Everything else authenticates automatically from there.
4. Run **05 · End Session → Logout** last — not before. See that folder's description for why.

## Auth model
Every request in this collection inherits collection-level auth: `Authorization: JWT {{authToken}}`, populated by the Login request's test script. This app is deliberately **not** cookie-friendly to non-browser clients: `src/payload.config.ts` sets a non-empty `csrf` allowlist, and Payload's cookie-auth strategy requires either an `Origin` header matching that allowlist or a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header — neither of which a plain HTTP client sends. The `JWT <token>` header sidesteps CSRF checking entirely. A collection-level pre-request script also stamps `Origin: {{baseUrl}}` on every request, so switching a request to cookie auth still works.

## Gotchas
- **IDs are integers** (Postgres adapter) — `banner`, `author`, and every `:id` path segment take a plain number.
- **`?locale=` only works on the two "Legacy wire-compat" requests.** `/api/posts` has no Payload localization configured; Korean/English are separate sibling fields (`title` vs `titleEn`, etc.).
- **Create responses are wrapped**: `{ message, doc: {...} }` — the new id is at `.doc.id`.
- **`publishedAt` isn't auto-stamped on create**, only on a later update while it's still empty — see "Publish Post".
- **Media upload is multipart** with JSON fields packed into a `_payload` text part, not plain form fields.
- **`POST`/`DELETE` on `/api/users` require `role: "admin"`.**
- **Anonymous reads of `/api/posts` are always filtered to `_status: "published"`**, regardless of any `where` you send.
- **A relationship id in a JSON body must be a bare number, not a quoted variable.** Postman substitutes variables as text, so `"{{mediaId}}"` becomes the string `"123"` — this API 400s that for `banner`/`author` (strict `typeof value === "number"` check, see `node_modules/payload/dist/utilities/isValidID.js`). "Create Post" writes `{{mediaId}}` unquoted for exactly this reason; copy that pattern for any other numeric field you template.
- **Logout ends the whole session, not just this token.** `useSessions: true` (Payload's default) means logout deletes the session server-side; the same JWT is then rejected everywhere, long before its 2-hour expiry. Keep "05 · End Session → Logout" last.

exec: // Every write needs Origin to equal NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL exactly, or
// Payload's CSRF check discards cookie-based auth and 403s. Harmless to
// send on GETs too, and keeps this collection working if a request's
// auth is ever switched from the header strategy to the cookie jar.

item.name: 00 · Auth
item.description:
Payload's built-in auth endpoints for the `users` collection (`auth: true` in `src/collections/Users.ts`).

**Run "Login" first** — its test script captures the JWT into the collection variable `authToken`, which every other request in this collection sends as `Authorization: JWT {{authToken}}` (set once, at the collection level, under this collection's Authorization tab).

Why a header and not the cookie Postman would normally store: this app sets a non-empty `csrf` allowlist (`src/payload.config.ts`), and Payload's cookie-auth strategy silently drops the token for any request that has neither an `Origin` header nor a `Sec-Fetch-Site` header — exactly what a plain HTTP client sends. The `JWT <token>` header bypasses that check entirely (`node_modules/payload/dist/auth/extractJWT.js`).

Logout lives in its own folder at the very end (`05 · End Session`), not here — see that folder's description for why order matters.

request.description:
Authenticates and returns `{ message, user, token, exp }`. `token` is a JWT valid for 2 hours; `user.role` (`admin`/`editor`) rides inside it because `role` has `saveToJWT: true` in `src/collections/Users.ts`.

The test script below saves `token` into the collection variable `authToken` so every subsequent request authenticates automatically.

**Body fields**
| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes |
| `password` | string | yes |

Seed credentials (see `src/seed/index.ts`): `admin@wsoftlabs.dev` / `changeme-admin-123` (role `admin`) and `editor@wsoftlabs.dev` / `changeme-editor-123` (role `editor`). The environment ships the admin pair as `adminEmail`/`adminPassword` so every write in this collection (which requires `admin`) works out of the box.

Returns the user matching the current `authToken`, or `{ user: null }` if unauthenticated/expired. Useful as a quick "is my token still good" check.

Response shape: `{ user: { id, name, email, role, ... }, token, exp, message }`.

item.name: 01 · Media
item.description:
The `media` upload collection (`src/collections/Media.ts`) — image library used for post banners. Reads are fully public; writes require an authenticated user.

**Run "Upload Media" first** in this folder — its test script captures the new doc's id into `mediaId`, which the Posts folder's "Create Post" request attaches as the post's `banner`.

There's no "Delete Media" request here: with a post attached to it via `banner`, deleting the media first would either fail the FK constraint or leave the post's banner dangling. That cleanup step lives at the end of `02 · Posts`, once the referencing post is gone.

formdata.description: The image file. Restricted to mimeTypes: image/* (src/collections/Media.ts).

JSON-encoded string of every non-file field on the doc. `alt` is required (src/collections/Media.ts). This `_payload` wrapper is how Payload accepts field data alongside a multipart file — plain form fields are not read.

request.description:
Uploads an image. **Select a file for the `file` form-data key before sending** — Postman collections can't embed binary content, so it isn't pre-filled.

Payload auto-generates `thumbnail` (400×300) and `banner` (1600×900) sized variants (`src/collections/Media.ts`) and returns their URLs under `doc.sizes`.

Response is wrapped: `{ message, doc: { id, url, filename, mimeType, filesize, width, height, sizes, alt, ... } }` — the id is at `.doc.id`, not `.id`.
Public — no auth required. Returns the standard Payload list envelope: `{ docs, totalDocs, page, totalPages, hasNextPage, hasPrevPage, ... }`.
Public — no auth required. 404s with `{ errors: [...] }` if the id doesn't exist.

Requires auth (default collection access — no explicit `update` rule in `src/collections/Media.ts`). Only non-file fields can be changed this way; to replace the file itself, re-upload.

**Body fields**
| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `alt` | string | yes (collection-required, but PATCH only needs the fields you're changing) |

item.name: 02 · Posts
item.description:
The `posts` collection (`src/collections/Posts.ts`) — the blog's core content type, with drafts/versions enabled.

**Bilingual content is NOT Payload localization.** `localization` is deliberately unconfigured — Korean lives in `title`/`content`/`excerpt`, English in the sibling `titleEn`/`contentEn`/`excerptEn` fields. `?locale=` has no effect on these endpoints (it only means something on the legacy `/api/getPosts` / `/api/getPost` routes in folder 04).

**Run "Create Post" first** in this folder — it attaches the media doc from folder 01 as `banner` and its test script captures `postId`/`postSlug` for every other request here. This folder's last request, "Delete Media", cleans up that media doc too (see its description for why it isn't in the Media folder).

request.description:
Requires auth (any logged-in user — `create: ({ req }) => Boolean(req.user)`).

**Body fields**
| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | **yes** | Korean/base title |
| `slug` | string | no | auto-slugified from `title` if omitted; must be unique |
| `content` | Lexical richText JSON | no | Korean/base body — see the raw body for the minimal shape |
| `excerpt` | string | no | Korean/base one-liner |
| `titleEn` / `contentEn` / `excerptEn` | same types | no | English counterparts; omitted here, so this post falls back to Korean for English readers |
| `banner` | integer | no | a `media` doc id — pre-filled from `{{mediaId}}` (folder 01). Left **unquoted** in the raw body on purpose: this API 400s a relationship id sent as a numeric string (`"123"`), so the variable must substitute to a bare JSON number (`123`). |
| `author` | integer | no | a `users` doc id |
| `_status` | `"draft"` \| `"published"` | no | drafts are never returned to anonymous readers |

**Gotcha**: `publishedAt` is only auto-stamped by a hook on *update*, not on create (`src/collections/Posts.ts`) — so creating directly with `_status: "published"` still leaves `publishedAt` null until the post is next saved. See "Publish Post" below, which sets it explicitly.

Response is wrapped: `{ message, doc: { id, ... } }`.

query.description: Field to sort by; prefix with - for descending.
Example filter — only visible to an authenticated user; anonymous reads are always forced to published.
Include the draft version of documents that have one, instead of only the last-published version.

request.description:
Anonymous callers only ever see `{ _status: { equals: "published" } }` docs, regardless of `where` — enforced server-side in `src/collections/Posts.ts`. Log in (folder 00) to also see drafts.

Returns the standard Payload list envelope: `{ docs, totalDocs, page, totalPages, hasNextPage, hasPrevPage, ... }`.
404s with `{ errors: [...] }` if the id doesn't exist or (for anonymous callers) isn't published.

query.description: 0 = return relationship ids only, no population.

request.description: `slug` is unique but is not the document id, so looking a post up by its URL slug means a `where` filter on the list endpoint rather than a direct `/api/posts/:id` call. Returns the list envelope — expect `docs.length` to be 0 or 1.

Requires auth. Flips the post live and stamps `publishedAt` explicitly — relying on the auto-stamp hook alone only works on an update where the value is still empty, so an explicit timestamp here is the reliable way to publish-with-a-date in one call.

**Body fields**
| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `_status` | `"draft"` \| `"published"` | no |
| `publishedAt` | ISO date string | no |

Once published, this post becomes visible to anonymous `GET` requests (List Posts, Find Post by Slug, and both legacy endpoints in folder 04).
Requires auth. Run this before "Delete Media" below — it's the post referencing that media doc as its `banner`.

Cleans up the media doc uploaded in `01 · Media`. Placed here, after "Delete Post" above, rather than in the Media folder — this post's `banner` pointed at it, so deleting the media first (while the post still referenced it) would fail or leave a dangling reference. Requires auth; also deletes the file from disk (`MEDIA_DIR`).

item.name: 03 · Users
item.description:
The `users` auth collection (`src/collections/Users.ts`). Two roles only: `editor` (write posts) and `admin` (also manages users).

Collection-level `read` is public (so a post byline/author name can be shown to anonymous readers), but the `email` and `role` fields individually require an authenticated caller — an anonymous `GET` sees `name` only.

**Run "Create User" first** in this folder (requires the admin token from folder 00) — its test script captures `userId` for the requests below.

request.description:
**Requires `role: "admin"`** — `create: ({ req }) => req.user?.role === "admin"`. An editor token gets a 403 here.

**Body fields**
| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | |
| `email` | string | yes | unique |
| `password` | string | yes | injected by `auth: true`; never returned in any response |
| `role` | `"editor"` \| `"admin"` | no | defaults to `"editor"`; only an admin may set/change it |

Response is wrapped: `{ message, doc: { id, ... } }` (no `token` — creating a user via this endpoint does not log in as them).

Public — no auth required, but each doc's `email` and `role` only appear when the request is authenticated (field-level access in `src/collections/Users.ts`). Compare this response logged out vs. logged in.
Same field-level visibility rule as List Users applies here.

An admin can update anyone; a non-admin can only update their own doc (`update: { id: { equals: req.user?.id } }` for everyone else). Changing `role` additionally requires `role === "admin"` regardless of whose doc it is.

**Body fields**
| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no |
| `role` | `"editor"` \| `"admin"` | no — admin-only to change |
**Requires `role: "admin"`** — same rule as Create User.

item.name: 04 · Legacy wire-compat
item.description:
Hand-written Next.js routes (`src/app/api/getPosts`, `src/app/api/getPost/[id]`) that reproduce the old Laravel `BlogController` response shape byte-for-byte, so `wsoftlabs-website-v2`'s Nuxt proxies (`server/api/getBlogs.get.js`, `getPost/[id].get.js`) can point at this app by only flipping an env var — no template changes on that side (see WOS-314).

These are **read-only, always public, and unrelated to the Payload REST API above**: field names are flat snake_case (`banner_url`, `published_at`), the list endpoint returns a bare JSON array (not the `{docs, ...}` envelope), and `?locale=` — meaningless on `/api/posts` — is exactly how these two routes choose Korean vs. English.

Requests below target `welcome-to-the-w-labs-blog`, a post created by `pnpm seed` (`src/seed/index.ts`) — reseed first if it's missing.

request.description: No `locale` param defaults to Korean (`src/lib/locale.ts`). Returns a bare array, capped at 50, sorted by `-publishedAt`, drafts excluded. Each item omits `content` (full body) to keep the list light — see "Legacy: Get Post by Slug" for that.

query.description: Accepted aliases: en. (ko/kr/ko-kr all map to Korean; anything else falls back to Korean too.)

request.description: Same endpoint as above with `?locale=en`. Any post missing an English translation (`titleEn` etc. empty) falls back to its Korean text field-by-field (`pick()` in `src/lib/locale.ts`) rather than being omitted.

Accepts either a numeric legacy id or a slug (`/^\d+$/` picks which) — this request uses the slug form. Unlike the list endpoint, the detail response includes `content` as a rendered **HTML string** (Lexical JSON converted server-side). 404 body on a miss: `{ "message": "Post not found." }`.

item.name: 05 · End Session
item.description:
Logout is deliberately last, in its own folder, and not grouped with Login in `00 · Auth`.

This app uses Payload's default `auth.useSessions: true`, which tracks each login as a session entry (keyed by a `sid` claim inside the JWT) on the user's own doc. Logout deletes that session server-side (`node_modules/payload/dist/auth/operations/logout.js`), and the JWT auth strategy checks the `sid` against the user's remaining sessions on every request (`node_modules/payload/dist/auth/strategies/jwt.js`) — so **the same token stops authenticating immediately after logout**, well before its 2-hour expiry. Run this after every other folder, or every write for the rest of the run will 403.

request.description: Ends the current session (pass `?allSessions=true` to end every session for this user instead of just this one). The response confirms with `{ message }`; the `authToken` variable still holds the now-rejected JWT until you Login again.
